Mold-specific intelligence, end to end.

Warm, humid rooms are mold's ideal habitat. Most dehumidifiers see one number, humidity. MoldGuard reads the full picture, humidity, temperature, exposure duration, and virtual dew point margin, adds weather foresight, and responds on its own.

01

Mold Risk Index engine

Real-time risk scoring built from humidity, temperature, and sustained exposure duration, with a virtual surface dew point calculation, going beyond the single-threshold triggers used by commercial dehumidifiers, and avoiding false triggers during temporary humidity spikes.

02

Environmental & VOC monitoring

An SGP40 VOC sensor adds supplementary air-quality context alongside humidity, temperature, and duration. We treat VOC as context, never standalone proof: research shows microbial VOC levels are often too low for reliable detection and easily confounded by household sources.

03

Predictive weather integration

Weather API forecasts are combined with indoor readings to anticipate humidity spikes and pre-dry spaces ahead of them.

04

Closed-loop auto-dehumidification

When the index crosses the risk threshold, the ESP32 switches a connected semiconductor dehumidifier on via a solid-state relay, and off once conditions return to safe range.

05

Water-tank monitoring

A time-of-flight sensor and magnetic reed switch track the removable tank's fill level, alerting you before overflow.

06

Web dashboard & analytics

Historical trend logging for humidity, temperature, and VOCs, with multi-room and multi-unit views for larger households, dormitories, or property managers.

07

Mobile alerts & control

Real-time push notifications as risk rises, live device status, and manual override of the dehumidification unit from anywhere.

Honest positioning.

Proactive, not reactive.

Existing options were built for general comfort or simple humidity control, not mold-specific risk modeling.

MoldGuard V1.0 (ours) Mold Risk Index (humidity + temperature + duration), supplementary VOC context, predictive weather integration, closed-loop auto-dehumidification, water-tank monitoring, web + mobile dashboard Fixed development fee Requires dedicated power source; periodic water-tank emptying

Sensible hardware, no black box.

Open, off-the-shelf components, expand a row for the plain-language spec.

Humidity & temperature sensing
SHT41 sensor module, high-accuracy temperature and relative humidity measurement for the risk engine's core inputs.
VOC / air-quality sensing
SGP40 VOC sensor, supplementary air-quality context, read alongside humidity, temperature, and duration, never as a standalone mold verdict.
Dehumidification unit
A Gaabor 2-in-1 semiconductor dehumidifier (1 L tank) is switched safely by an SSR-40DA solid-state relay: the ESP32's low-voltage logic controls 220 V AC mains with strict electrical isolation. A VL53L0X time-of-flight sensor and magnetic reed switch monitor tank fill and seating.
Brain & connectivity
ESP32-WROOM-32 (dual-core, WiFi + Bluetooth) publishes telemetry and receives commands over MQTT via HiveMQ Cloud, on a pipeline built to stay stable under fluctuating network conditions.
Enclosure & placement
Sensors and controller mount in a compact ABS housing (1×200×300 mm boards) attached to the dehumidifier, with a removable 1 L tank you empty when the app tells you it's full.
Software stack
React + Tailwind web dashboard on Vercel, React Native mobile app, Node.js/Express + TypeScript backend on Render, PostgreSQL (Neon) history store, MQTT via HiveMQ Cloud, and Socket.IO real-time sync to clients.

From invisible risk to handled, automatically.

MoldGuard runs a continuous loop: monitor the room, score the real mold risk, and act before conditions turn into growth, informed by the weather forecast too.

The closed loop: sense → score → act → report

01

Sense

Humidity, temperature, VOC
02

Score

The risk engine
03

Act

Dehumidifier on auto
04

Report

Dashboard and alerts
1

Sense the room, continuously.

A sensor pod watches the conditions mold actually cares about: relative humidity, temperature, and volatile organic compounds (VOCs). The SHT41 measures the risk engine's core inputs; VOCs add supplementary context, read together with everything else rather than as a verdict.
2

Score the risk, not just a number.

The Mold Risk Index combines humidity, temperature, and how long those conditions persist, instead of reacting to a single humidity threshold. That's what makes the prediction early: it catches the window where mold can start, before it does. Outdoor forecast data sharpens that window further.

Closet 82% RH 26h sustained Dew point margin −0.4°C
3

Act: dehumidify, no hands.

When the index crosses the risk threshold, the ESP32 switches the connected semiconductor dehumidifier on through a solid-state relay and pulls moisture back down, closing the loop without you touching anything. Extracted water collects in the removable 1 L tank, monitored so you're told before it's full.

4

Report: see everything, anywhere.

Live status and historical trends stream to the web dashboard over real-time sync; the mobile app pushes an alert the moment risk rises, and lets you override the unit manually from anywhere.

Straight answers.

Do I still need a dehumidifier?
MoldGuard works with its paired semiconductor dehumidifier: the risk engine switches it on and off automatically. The system pairs with the Gaabor dehumidifier specified in the quote.
What maintenance does it need?
Periodic emptying of the 1 L water tank (you get an alert before it's full) and a dedicated power source: that's the honest list, straight from our own comparison table.
Does it work without the internet?
The device buffers readings locally when connectivity drops and syncs once reconnected; cloud services (MQTT broker, dashboard, database) run hosted, so there's nothing to maintain on your machine.
How much does it cost?
MoldGuard builds its intelligence around an off-the-shelf dehumidifier with open, individually-sourced components: a fixed, itemized hardware cost, a single fixed development fee, full client ownership, and only minimal, predictable cloud service costs at small scale. Exact figures come from the team's quote, not published on the site.
Who is it for?
Renters, households, dormitories, and small property managers: anyone who wants affordable, vendor-agnostic mold monitoring without a building-management system built for towers.
